platforms.policy: bin/install refuses any platform not listed in published, before downloading anything, and prints what is available. 'planned' gets a different message than 'unsupported', so an ARM user arriving early learns the platform is coming rather than assuming the project is dead. published is the single source of truth: bin/install's SUPPORTED variable and the README 'Platform support' table must both match it, and scripts/test.sh T3e asserts that they do.
platforms.rosetta: darwin-arm64 falls back to the darwin-x86_64 artifact through Rosetta 2 when no native arm64 build exists. One Intel artifact therefore covers both Intel Macs and Apple Silicon, which halves the macOS build matrix. The fallback is skipped as soon as a native darwin-arm64 artifact is published.
platforms.darwin_caveat: macOS builds cannot bundle system libraries the way Linux can: libSystem and libc++ are supplied by the OS, so a macOS artifact is tied to its MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET (11.0) and is not fully self-contained. Non-system dependencies are bundled and referenced through @loader_path rpath with install_name_tool, and every rewritten Mach-O is re-signed ad-hoc because arm64 refuses an invalid signature.
platforms.legacy_note: 5.4.45 and 5.6.40 have no linux-arm64 target and never will: their base is debian:jessie, whose official multi-arch index carries only 386/amd64/armv5/armv7 (verified with docker buildx imagetools on 2026-11-08). Moving to a base that has arm64 would raise glibc from 2.19 to 2.24/2.31, which is exactly the property those two versions exist for. bin/install reports this as unavailable for that version, not as planned.

checksum_policy: sha256 must be a 64-char lowercase hex string or null. null means NOT BUILT. Never invent a checksum. Build inputs use FILL:<filename> placeholders in versions/*.toml and are filled only by scripts/vendor.sh from bytes it actually downloaded.

generations.notes: 与 G1 的关键区别：这一代不需要 vendor OpenSSL，也不需要符号隔离 —— PHP 与系统库用的是同一份 libssl.so.1.1，冲突前提不存在，curl 不必换 GnuTLS。7.2/7.3 在 GCC 10 上需要 -fcommon（-fno-common 自 GCC 10 成为默认，否则链接期 multiple definition）；7.4+ mbstring 需 libonig-dev。
8.4+ 要求 OpenSSL >=1.1.1 且 <4.0。8.1.34 已于 2025-12-31 EOL，故作为闭集末版一并冻结。与 G2 的 flag 差异：8.1 起 GD 开关是 --enable-gd（--with-gd 只警告不生效，结果是 gd 静默缺席），sodium 默认启用需 libsodium-dev。

support_matrix.template_rationale: 按 OpenSSL ABI 代际切成 3 套 Dockerfile 模板即可覆盖全部支持范围，而不是每个版本写一个。三套共用 scripts/pack-artifact.sh（自包含 / 重定位 / 搬路径自检 / 打包），平台差异只在那一处维护。

platform_policy.linux: 每个版本都出 x86_64 与 arm64。arm64 必须用原生 runner（GitHub ubuntu-24.04-arm），QEMU 下编 PHP 要数小时且会掩盖真实失败。
platform_policy.darwin: 5.x 与 7.2-7.4 只出 darwin-x86_64（覆盖 Intel 原生 + Apple Silicon 经 Rosetta 2）；8.0/8.1+ 额外出 darwin-arm64 原生，因为现代项目的主力机器是 Apple Silicon。
platform_policy.why_not_more: darwin-arm64 的 5.4/5.6 需要给 2014 年代的 C 代码打大量补丁（Zend 里 __aarch64__ 分支为 0，内联汇编虽有纯 C fallback，但现代 Clang 对这批代码极严），收益远小于成本 —— 这类用户本来就极少，且 Rosetta 已经能覆盖。

extension_tiers._source: WSL Surý apt 实测（2026-11-08 mise 迁移验收日志）作为分档锚点；跨版本的收敛选择见 values
extension_tiers.rationale: 刻意收敛成 4 份扩展源码而不是 14 份：phpredis 2.2.8 只给 PHP 5.x，5.3.7 覆盖 7.0-8.2；swoole 1.10.5 只给 5.x，4.8.13 覆盖 7.2-8.2。版本矩阵越大，扩展源码份数越该收敛，否则每份都是一次独立的编译风险。

caveats: planned 不等于 published：每铺通一个平台才改 manifest 的 status + 加一行 versions.txt（每个版本只加一次，第一次发布时）。
2026-10 官方对 7.4 / 8.0 / 8.1 等 EOL 分支发过源码级安全 backport（PHP2Shell）。冻结源选型时需决定用 museum/php.net 末版 tarball 还是官方 backport；制品默认带 INSECURE / offline-only 标签。
G2/G3 的 base digest 目前是 REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST 占位，必须先用 scripts/pin-base.sh 解析出同时含 linux/amd64 与 linux/arm64 的 index digest；l2.sh 在构建前会校验 digest 是否覆盖目标平台。

notes: extensions.redis = 2.2.8: phpredis 2.x is the last branch for PHP < 7 (official 2.2.8 release notes). phpredis 6.3.0 requires PHP >= 7.4.0 per PECL, so it cannot be reused for 5.4. Verified 2026-11-08.

extensions.swoole = 1.10.5 is the last 1.x release (2018-05-14). L2 2026-11-08 实测：在 PHP 5.4.45 上 phpize / configure / make 全通过，swoole.so 与 redis.so 都已装入制品（构建日志 #10 的 php -m 同时列出两者）。Dockerfile 仍保留 soft-fail 兜底，但 smoke 已把扩展缺失升级为硬 FAIL。

vendor/*.tar.gz and vendor/SOURCES.json are the only frozen build inputs: scripts/vendor.sh --write produces them once, they are committed, and CI re-verifies each sha256. keys/jessie.gpg is gone (2026-11-08) — it lived under .gitignore, so a fresh clone never had the file and Dockerfile.g1 / Dockerfile.5.4 died on that COPY line with an error unrelated to the real cause. The jessie archive key is expired anyway, so build/apt-install.sh starts jessie/stretch directly in [trusted=yes].

base digest resolved 2026-11-08 from WSL 'docker buildx imagetools inspect debian:jessie': sha256:32ad5050caffb2c7e969dac873bce2c370015c2256ff984b70c1c08b3a2816a0. Docker Hub was unreachable from the Windows host, so this value was not independently re-verified there. Mirroring to a self-hosted registry (GC protection) is a V1 wrap-up step, not an L2 prerequisite.

artifact layout (2026-11-08): self-contained. jessie-only sonames are enumerated via ldd and bundled into lib/; bin/php is a wrapper setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH to that dir, with the real ELF at libexec/php.bin; the glibc family is deliberately excluded so the host's newer libc is used. curl links GnuTLS (libcurl4-gnutls-dev) so it cannot collide with the vendored OpenSSL 1.0.2u over the shared libssl.so.1.0.0 soname.

SSL isolation contract (2026-11-08 L2): the vendored OpenSSL 1.0.2u serves ext/openssl only. Debian's libssl.so.1.0.0 exports versioned SSL_*@OPENSSL_1.0.0 symbols that upstream 1.0.2u lacks, so any jessie system library needing them must stay out of the final link line. Two measured cases: libcurl (switched to GnuTLS) and libpq (pdo_pgsql and libpq-dev removed after 40+ undefined references at link time). Legacy business projects are MySQL-only, and this is an offline migration tool, so trimming the frozen feature set beats mixing two SSL chains. scripts/test.sh T3b guards this.

support scope frozen 2026-11-08: 5.4 / 5.6 / 7.2 / 7.3 / 7.4 / 8.0 / 8.1+. All concrete branches are already EOL, so their last releases become a 7-version frozen closed set; 8.2+ rolls through the current channel. 3 Dockerfile templates (g1 5.x / g2 7.2-8.0 / g3 8.1+) cover the whole range. See support_matrix for sources and per-generation constraints.

relocation fix (2026-11-08 L2): the first green build shipped redis.so, swoole.so and their conf.d ini files, yet smoke reported both extensions NOT loaded. Root cause was NOT a build failure: --with-config-file-scan-dir and extension_dir were compiled as absolute /opt/php/5.4.45 paths, so an unpacked artifact never scanned conf.d and could not resolve the .so files. scripts/relocate.sh now injects PHPRC, PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR and ASDF_PHP_PREFIX via bin/php / php-cgi wrappers, writes conf.d/00-relocatable.ini with extension_dir=${ASDF_PHP_PREFIX}/... (PHP 5.4 supports ${VAR} ini interpolation: Zend/zend_ini_parser.y:357 cfg_var_ref), and strips hardcoded prefixes from phpize / php-config / pear / pecl / peardev / phar. Published 2026-11-08 as x-rush/asdf-php Releases tag php-5.4.45 (target branch v2) with sha256 21b9a98ab9cda5a23d65cd36e8be8b9a4548d05473e668a623eb45f59302f3b4.

full-matrix scaffolding (2026-11-08): scripts/pack-artifact.sh was extracted so g1/g2/g3 and the macOS path share one packaging implementation (bundle runtime libs, relocate, move-the-prefix self-check, tar+sha256). Duplicating those 160 lines per template was the main drift risk. Platform-specific parts are explicit: ldd vs otool -L, glibc family excluded on Linux, /usr/lib and /System excluded on macOS, install_name_tool + @loader_path rpath + ad-hoc codesign on macOS.

configure-flag drift is silent, so it is now gated twice: scripts/gen-build-inputs.py refuses flags that are wrong for a version at build-input time (--with-mysql before 7.0; zip is --enable-zip until 7.4 and --with-zip from 7.4; gd is --with-gd until 7.4 and --enable-gd from 7.4; --with-freetype-dir/--with-jpeg-dir until 7.4; any /opt/toolchain path in g2/g3), and scripts/smoke-artifact.sh runs a runtime feature probe (mbstring, curl, gd jpeg+png, mysqli, pdo_mysql, openssl, zip, zlib) because a wrong flag only produces an 'unrecognized options' warning and an artifact that runs but silently lacks functions.

build dependencies are the one input this repository cannot pin (2026-11-08): for an EOL suite the live mirror still serves its index but has deleted the files that index names — bullseye-security pointed at perl 5.32.1-4+deb11u5, gcc-10 10.2.1-6 and libicu67 while all three returned 404, so apt-get update succeeds and install dies at 4 of 47 packages. build/apt-install.sh therefore skips deb.debian.org for jessie/stretch/buster/bullseye, walks the domestic archive mirrors and then archive.debian.org, keeps apt's partial download cache across attempts and resumes with --fix-missing instead of refetching 70 MB. Measured inside this Docker host: bullseye 102 MB / 101 s, jessie 74.3 MB / 123 s. A proxy or internal mirror overrides the whole chain with --build-arg APT_MIRROR_MAIN.

macOS platform reality (2026-11-08, source-verified): Zend in PHP 5.4.45 has zero __aarch64__ branches and three __x86_64__ ones (zend_operators.h, zend_multiply.h, zend_alloc.c), all inline assembly with plain-C fallbacks and no #error on unknown architectures, so arm64 is not architecturally blocked. The real obstacles are the macOS SDK (no curl headers, no OpenSSL headers), modern Clang diagnostics (implicit function declaration is an error since Clang 15), and the impossibility of bundling libSystem. Hence: 5.x and 7.2-7.4 ship darwin-x86_64 only (covering Apple Silicon via Rosetta 2), 8.0/8.1 add native darwin-arm64.
